title: Card population registry v1
description: WHICH CARDS A COMPILER MAY READ, AND FOR WHAT. Authored by 0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform~X to 4.0.0_SA_CRO~A's admission ruling. It exists because a GLOB WAS BEING USED AS AN AUTHORITY BOUNDARY: `CARD_GLOB` had a wave number baked into it, so the compiler's honest '0 exact matches' was a true statement about its own configuration that every reader took as a statement about the estate (doctrine principle 13). A registry moves admission from a pattern that silently changes meaning each wave to an ENUMERATION that can only change by being edited. PLACED IN THE COMPILER'S OWN DELIVERABLE DIRECTORY, NOT org/standards/: this is a lane artifact proposed for promotion, and promoting it is 4.0.0_SA_CRO~A's act, not mine.

registry_version.description: Pinned. A consumer branches on this before reading anything else.

ratified_at_commit.description: The commit whose CARD_GLOB result this registry RATIFIES. v1's extension population is exactly what that glob admitted at that commit -- a one-time hand-off from pattern to enumeration, recorded so nobody later reads the enumeration as independently derived.

extension_population.description: The cards feeding the EXISTING W3 map/enrich path, and nothing else. Membership here says NOTHING about receiver-source eligibility.

receiver_source_populations.description: THREE INDEPENDENT POPULATIONS, one per receiver, keyed separately. ⛔ NOT one role enum: 4.0.0_SA_CRO~A withdrew that and the reason is load-bearing -- extension participation and receiver-source participation are INDEPENDENT CONSUMER DIMENSIONS, and one card may lawfully sit in several. A single role field would have made the lawful case unrepresentable.

discovery_globs.description: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. A consumer may use these to REPORT candidates that are not admitted; it may never admit anything because a glob matched. This field exists so the demotion is written down rather than remembered -- an unwritten demotion is the protection that exists only as a description.

sha256.description: Full digest of the file's RAW BYTES. Not a truncation: a shortened digest is a different claim wearing the same name.

repo_relative_path.description: Forward slashes, no leading slash, no dot segments, no doubled separators, no drive letter, no whitespace.

subject_id.description: The card's own subject.id, PINNED HERE TOO. Path and digest identify the FILE; this identifies WHAT IT IS ABOUT, and a card whose subject changed under an unchanged path is exactly the substitution a digest catches only by accident.

members.description: EXACT membership. An empty array is the claim 'nothing is admitted here', which a consumer can branch on.

EMPTY IN v1 FOR ALL THREE, BY CONTRACT AND NOT BY OVERSIGHT. No schema-bound card-to-L0 transform exists; `key` additionally has no key_expression field in SUBSTRATE_CARD.v2 and `grain` has no authored projection in any card. An empty role that a later reader mistakes for an unfinished one is the failure this description exists to prevent.

transform_version.description: The pinned version of the card-to-L0 transform that produced these members. NULL is legal ONLY alongside an empty members array -- a member admitted without a transform pin is a value with no provenance, and two members carrying different pins in one population is a population that cannot replay.

declared_branch_predicate.description: The exact condition a card must satisfy to be admitted as a source for THIS receiver. Written out rather than referenced, because 'incomplete receiver payload cannot admit' is unactionable until someone says what complete means.

allOf.$comment: no transform pin => no members. The converse (members => a pin) follows from the pattern on the string form.
